perspective:
I, Sara Manuelito, have access to the following:

- I am a Speech-Language Pathologist. Shirley Whiteplume is a nurse, a long-time colleague, and close friend; we have worked together at a community health center for several years.
- I attended the funeral of a mutual patient. I observed Shirley looking somber and suspected she was deeply affected by the loss.
- I told Shirley I knew it was hard for her and that I saw how much she cared for him. I heard her say it had been tough and that she kept thinking something more could have been done.
- I told her we did everything we could and should remember the good care and moments of joy. She said I was right but that it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, I brought up our treatment decisions because I sensed she felt burdened. She told me she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped.
- I told her we made the best decisions with the information we had and that she should not carry the burden alone. She said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- I observed Shirley continuing to be reserved and showing minimal emotion. In a quiet moment in our office, I told her she had been holding back her feelings and that it was okay to be open.
- She told me she was not sure she could and did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. I told her showing emotion does not make her weak and is healthy among friends. She said maybe I was right and she would try.
- Later, I felt my previous confrontation might have been too harsh, so I apologized. She said it had been a bit much but that she knew I meant well and appreciated the apology.
- I told her I was there for her however she needed. She thanked me and said we should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, I noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better. I asked how she felt. She said she was feeling better thanks to our talks and my support.
- I suggested spending more time together outside work. She agreed, and we planned something for the weekend.
- I know that Shirley and I made the patient’s treatment decisions together and used the information available to us at the time.
- I felt hopeful when I noticed Shirley’s improvement and offered further support.
